gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-phoen: Urban and commanding, Capture It stands tall and nearly sealed, every stroke the same width. Noto Sans Phoenician is the open one, with generous lowercase and curves that spread wide.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-psalt: Capture It is built like bent wire, tall in the lowercase with its letters almost shut. Then Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi loosens everything, with gaping mouths on the e and capitals that hardly rise, so a modest size is plenty.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-rejan: Wide glass portholes in the lowercase give this body font a bright, see-through look. Noto Sans Rejang keeps c, e, s and a clearly open, while Capture It stays towering and nearly sealed up top.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-runic: Noto Sans Runic reads big and tightly packed, with curves that never close back on themselves. Under Capture It, whose rounds and stems all share one weight, a long page would feel dense yet unclosed.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-samar: Noto Sans Samaritan has hefty lowercase with plenty of daylight inside every curve, which makes it feel friendly and approachable. Capture It is the tube-like one, holding its thickness through each bend.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-saura: Capture It towers over everything, its line thickness unvarying and its letters nearly sealed shut. Noto Sans Saurashtra does the opposite job, with counters that stay connected to the outside and capitals barely taller than their neighbors.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-sc: Noto Sans SC draws chalky curves that stop well short of closing. Capture It sits above it with a towering x-height and no calligraphic thinning, so the two meet as sealed against open.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-shara: Capture It is all towering x-height, with openings so slight its letters feel nearly sealed. Noto Sans Sharada, with open c forms and bulky lowercase proportions, can take a slightly smaller size without losing presence.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-siddh: Tall, tight and sealed up. Capture It keeps stroke widths fixed from stem to curve, and Noto Sans Siddham reads easily over a long page, with a large central band and an s whose ends hang far from the spine.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-sinha: Capture It has a towering x-height and curves that nearly seal themselves shut. But Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe through each line, so shrinking the heading would let that body overpower it.
